content: # Devin Docs > This file is very large and may be truncated. For an index of this content, please refer to https://docs.devin.ai/llms.txt instead. # Billing Source: https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing Devin has two pricing models: * **Self-serve**: Free, Pro, Max, and Teams plans you can sign up for directly at [app.devin.ai](https://app.devin.ai). Self-serve usage is billed through a mix of included quota and on-demand credits. See [Self-serve plans](/admin/billing/self-serve) for full details. * **Enterprise**: Devin Enterprise customers are billed in Agent Compute Units (ACUs) at the rate set in their order form. See [Enterprise](/admin/billing/enterprise) for how ACU consumption is tracked, or [contact sales](https://cognition.com/contact) for pricing. For how Devin meters work in general (how usage accrues, idle/sleep behavior, and tips for keeping consumption under control), see [Usage](/admin/billing/usage). The tips on that page apply to both pricing models. # Budgets Source: https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/budgets Learn how enterprise budgets form an ACU limit tree, set monthly windows and per-budget user tiers, and manage budgets with the API. Budgets let you cap ACU usage the way your company is organized: one limit for the account, shared pools for teams or projects, and per-user limits inside each pool. ## Sample use cases ### Departments with delegated admins Acme Corp has 10 departments. Each department head manages the limits of their orgs. Central IT sets each department's total. This example shows two of them. Alice, the enterprise admin, creates a budget for each department under the Account budget. She shares each one with its department admin. Each department admin creates a budget for each of their orgs. ![Account budget of 100,000 ACU with Engineering at 30,000 ACU, with Payments and Search, and Marketing at 5,000 ACU.](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/budget-departments.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=fd65b7ebd17f98f03e694dae32493b69) Department budgets under the Account budget * Bob, the Engineering department admin, can set limits and temporary limits on any budget under Engineering. For example, he can give Payments a temporary 6,000 ACU limit for a busy week. * Bob cannot raise Engineering's 30,000 ACU limit. Only Alice can. * Usage in every Engineering org counts toward the 30,000 ACU limit, even when the org budgets add up to more. ![Budgets page as a department admin](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/dept-admin-tree.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=9f921d3d02cf54e6a28792beb1db26b5) The Budgets page as a department admin, with the Account budget locked ![Raising a child budget limit](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/dept-admin-edit-child.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=a12442bc7a00464d08283bad62358864) A department admin raising a child budget limit ![Department budget limit is read-only](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/dept-admin-own-limit.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=7fc6e5bf029581de28e3290e6beb7554) A department admin cannot change the department budget limit ### A project bucket with higher user limits Every developer gets 200 ACUs a month. For the migration initiative, Acme Corp sets aside 5,000 ACUs and lets people on the project use more. Keep the Developer tools orgs in a Developer tools budget with a 200 ACU default tier. Create a Migration initiative budget with a 5,000 ACU limit. Put the project's org in it, and give it a 1,000 ACU default tier. Both budgets sit under the Account budget. ![Developer tools at 20,000 ACU with a 200 ACU default tier, and Migration initiative at 5,000 ACU with a 1,000 ACU default tier.](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/budget-project.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=a0d7477384a985d998a72ef8ae73f481) Developer tools and Migration initiative budgets with their tiers * Carol, a developer on the project, can use up to 1,000 ACUs in the Migration org. She can use up to 200 ACUs in the Developer tools orgs. * The whole project can never use more than 5,000 ACUs in a month. ![My Analytics budget picker](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/my-analytics-multi-budget.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=1b91652d38ed08edbcba1468f074af59) My Analytics budget picker with several budgets ## How budgets work ### Budget tree Each enterprise account has one budget tree. The root is the **Account budget**, and child budgets sit under it. A tree can be up to three levels deep. A budget can hold one organization or several. Each organization belongs to exactly one budget. New organizations go under the Account budget. For example, Acme Corp sets a 100,000 ACU limit on its Account budget. Engineering splits its pool into three child budgets. ![Account budget of 100,000 ACU with Engineering at 40,000 ACU, its three child budgets, and Developer tools at 20,000 ACU with three user limit tiers.](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/budget-tree.svg?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=48dc89ce8cd22e3043b576e5349ce1e0) Budget tree with budgets and user limit tiers Tiers are per-user limits inside one budget, not separate budgets. ![Budget tree with utilization per budget](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/tree.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=cc09209e5169718deadade894b7b4802) Budget tree with utilization per budget (mock data) ### Budget limits A budget limit caps the combined ACU usage of the budget's orgs and the orgs in its child budgets, for one monthly window. A `null` limit means unlimited. * **Usage counts toward every ancestor.** Usage in a child budget also counts toward its parent and the Account budget. * **An exhausted ancestor blocks its children.** When any budget on the path runs out, usage in that branch stops. * **Child limits can add up to more than the parent limit.** The parent limit still caps their combined usage. * **A budget with no limit is still capped by its parents.** A budget linked to exactly one organization shares its limit with that organization. The [organization-level ACU limit endpoints](/api-reference/v3/acu-limits/set-org-devin-acu-limit) remain supported and set it too. You can also use the [update endpoint](#update-a-budget) below. ### What happens when a budget runs out When a budget runs out, usage stops for its orgs. Usage also stops when any parent budget runs out. Usage resumes in the next monthly window, or when an admin raises the limit or sets a temporary limit. * **Devin sessions:** new sessions cannot start, and running sessions sleep. Users see "Increase your organization's usage limit." * **Devin CLI and Desktop local agent:** requests are blocked. Users see "Your organization has reached its monthly usage limit. Ask an account admin to raise it, or wait for the limit to reset next month." * **Devin Review:** full reviews stop. Automatic reviews and reviews started from the Devin Review page fall back to a diff-only analysis with no findings. Re-runs, reviews started through the API, and Review chat are rejected. ![Composer banner: usage limit reached](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/cloud-limit-reached.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=419babb34f9e136d7cd10853b3d18074) Composer banner when the budget is used up ### Monthly window Budget limits, user limits, and temporary limits reset at the start of each monthly window. Each window starts on the start day of your billing phase. It is not always the calendar month. For example, if the billing phase starts on the 15th, the windows run from October 15 to November 14, then from November 15 to December 14. A **temporary limit** replaces the budget limit for the rest of the current window. The permanent limit returns in the next window. A temporary user override expires at the end of the current window. ![Marketing budget with a temporary limit](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/limits-temporary.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=f5394365ee93dd0a9107ec8d650e8a93) A temporary limit raises Marketing to 6,000 ACUs for this window only ### User limits in a budget User limits cap how much one person can use in a monthly window. Each budget with a linked organization has its own user limits, and they apply within that budget only. > [!NOTE] > > If your enterprise still uses account-wide user limits, see [Migrating from account-wide user limits](#migrating-from-account-wide-user-limits) for how to move them to budgets. * **Tiers.** Each budget has its own tiers and one default tier. A tier sets the monthly ACU limit for its members. * **IdP group mappings.** Map an identity provider group to a tier. Members of the group get that tier. * **Overrides.** Set a permanent or a temporary limit for one user. * **Request policies.** Each tier sets how limit-increase requests are handled. `unconditional` and `conditional` approve requests up to the tier's `max_limit`. `manual` sends requests to an admin for review. * **Scope.** A user limit counts only the user's usage in that budget's orgs. * **Copy and clear.** Copy tiers from another budget or the account. You can also copy IdP group mappings, assignments, and overrides. Clear all tiers in a budget to start over. > [!WARNING] > > A user limit on a parent budget does not cover its child budgets. For example, if Engineering also holds an org, a 300 ACU user limit on Engineering does not cap a user's usage in Payments or Search. ![Copy usage policies dialog](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/copy-policies.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=bafda52c62081f5c5d3d71266eff8cad) Copy usage policies dialog with Developer tools as the source ### Who can manage a budget Enterprise admins manage budgets in **Enterprise Settings** under **Budgets**. They manage the whole tree, including the Account budget. * **Delegation.** An enterprise admin can share a budget with a person or group in the Manage access tab. A delegated admin can create budgets under it, and set limits and temporary limits on those child budgets. Delegation requires separate enablement; reach out to your account team. * **A delegated admin cannot raise the shared budget's own limit.** Only an admin who manages the parent budget can change it. * **Members** see their own usage and limit in My Analytics. ![Manage access tab of the Engineering budget](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL/images/admin/budgets/dept-admin-access.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=_lCZXv8Jkk2Nq1kL\&q=85\&s=a90c02116678e594ff6dfef6511b6724) Manage access tab of the Engineering budget, with Bob as a manager ## Frequently asked questions > [accordion] Can org admins set an org's ACU limit? > > No. Enterprise admins set org ACU limits. To let a team manage its own limits, share a budget with the team's admin. > [accordion] Why does the org-limit endpoint return 409? > > Once budget limits are enforced for your enterprise, the org-limit endpoint returns HTTP `409` when the org shares its budget with other orgs, or when it sits directly in the Account budget. The error reads "This organization has no limit of its own. Set the limit on its budget." For example, if Globex, Initech, and Umbrella share one budget, a limit write for Globex returns `409`. > [accordion] What happens to the older user-limit endpoints? > > After your enterprise switches to per-budget user limits, the older endpoints keep answering but change meaning: > > * Endpoints that take a user and no budget (`/v3beta1/enterprise/usage-policies/users/{user_id}`, `/v3beta1/enterprise/users/{user_id}/consumption/acu-limits`) set that user's limit in one budget only: the budget of the user's billing organization. The user's limits in other budgets do not change. If that organization has no budget, the call returns `409`. > * The account-wide tier, IdP group, and default user limit endpoints (`/v3beta1/enterprise/usage-policies/tiers`, `/idp-groups`, `/v3beta1/enterprise/users/consumption/acu-limits`) still edit your account-wide tiers, which are no longer enforced. > > Use the [budget-scoped endpoints](#tier-endpoints) below to manage every budget. > [accordion] Can a budget have separate cloud and local limits? > > No. A budget has one limit for cloud and local usage together. If your organizations have separate cloud and local limits, your account team combines them before your budgets are created. > [accordion] When do limits reset? > > At the start of each monthly window. The window starts on the start day of your billing phase. > [accordion] Can an org be in two budgets? > > No. Each org belongs to exactly one budget. A budget can hold many orgs. ## Manage budgets with the V3 API All requests authenticate with an enterprise **service user token**. Callers need the **ManageAcuLimits** account permission or [delegated access](#who-can-manage-a-budget) to the budget. Use `https://api.devin.ai` as the base URL. See the [V3 API overview](/api-reference/v3/overview) for authentication and service user guidance. Budget-scoped collection endpoints take the budget in the path: `/v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/...`. Endpoints that address a single tier or request (`/tiers/{tier_id}`, `/requests/{request_id}`) resolve the budget from the tier or request. On `/v3` they return HTTP `404` for an account-wide tier or request; those stay on `/v3beta1` (see [User-level ACU limits](/admin/billing/user-acu-limits)). Every endpoint on this page also answers on the same path under `/v3beta1`. ### PATCH semantics For the `PATCH` endpoints: * An omitted field is unchanged. * A field set to `null` is cleared. * A field set to a value is created or updated. ## Budget endpoints ### List budgets ```http theme={null} GET /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets ``` Returns a paginated list of the account's budgets, active and archived. Each budget looks like: ```json theme={null} { "budget_id": "budget-abc123", "name": "Engineering", "parent_budget_id": "budget-root", "org_ids": ["org-xyz789"], "status": "active", "cycle_acu_limit": 2000, "temporary_cycle_acu_limit": null } ``` * `budget_id`: the identifier to use in budget-scoped paths. * `parent_budget_id`: the parent budget; `null` for the account's root budget. * `org_ids`: the organizations linked to this budget. Their usage counts against it. Empty when no organization is linked. * `status`: `active` or `archived`. * `cycle_acu_limit`: the budget's limit on the ACU consumption charged to it and its descendants per monthly billing window; `null` means unlimited. * `temporary_cycle_acu_limit`: a limit that overrides `cycle_acu_limit` until the end of the current monthly billing window; `null` when none is live. ### Update a budget ```http theme={null} PATCH /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id} ``` Partial update; omitted fields are unchanged and `null` clears a limit. At least one field is required. * `parent_budget_id`: moves the budget, with its sub-budgets, under another active budget. The root budget cannot be moved, and budgets nest at most three levels deep. * `cycle_acu_limit`, `temporary_cycle_acu_limit`: the budget's limits, as in the list response. **Request body — set the limit and a temporary bump for this month** ```json theme={null} { "cycle_acu_limit": 2000, "temporary_cycle_acu_limit": 2500 } ``` **Request body — remove the limits** ```json theme={null} { "cycle_acu_limit": null, "temporary_cycle_acu_limit": null } ``` **Request body — move the budget under another budget** ```json theme={null} { "parent_budget_id": "budget-platform" } ``` Returns the updated budget. Setting `temporary_cycle_acu_limit` again restarts it for the current window. For a budget linked to exactly one organization, `cycle_acu_limit` also becomes the organization's ACU limit. ## Tier endpoints ### List tiers ```http theme={null} GET /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/tiers ``` Returns a paginated list of the budget's tiers in precedence order: highest `priority` first, newest tier first within a priority. Each tier looks like: ```json theme={null} { "tier_id": "tier-abc123", "name": "Engineers", "is_default": true, "cycle_acu_limit": 500, "policy": "manual", "max_limit": null, "priority": 0, "member_count": 42, "created_at": 1735689600 } ``` * `is_default`: whether this is the budget's default tier. * `cycle_acu_limit`: the default per-cycle ACU limit for each member; `null` means uncapped. * `policy`: how limit-increase requests against the tier are handled — `unconditional` and `conditional` approve up to `max_limit`, `manual` requires admin review. * `max_limit`: the maximum limit to which increase requests are approved; `null` approves without a ceiling. Always `null` when `cycle_acu_limit` is `null`. * `priority`: ranks the tier among a user's IdP-group-mapped tiers — the highest value wins, ties broken by newest tier. An explicit user assignment overrides the ranking, and the default tier never ranks. * `member_count`: the number of users currently in the tier. For the default tier this counts every budget member not in another tier. ### Create a tier ```http theme={null} POST /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/tiers ``` **Request body** ```json theme={null} { "name": "Engineers", "cycle_acu_limit": 500, "policy": "manual" } ``` The budget's first tier automatically becomes its default tier. Returns HTTP `201` with the created tier. ### Get a tier ```http theme={null} GET /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/tiers/{tier_id} ``` ### Update a tier ```http theme={null} PATCH /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/tiers/{tier_id} ``` Partial update; omitted fields are unchanged. ```json theme={null} { "name": "Engineering", "cycle_acu_limit": 750 } ``` ### Delete a tier ```http theme={null} DELETE /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/tiers/{tier_id} ``` Returns HTTP `204` on success. The default tier cannot be deleted (promote another tier first). A tier that still has users must have them moved first, and any IdP group mappings to the tier must be removed first. ## Tier user endpoints ### List a tier's users ```http theme={null} GET /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/tiers/{tier_id}/users ``` Returns a paginated list of the tier's users with their resolved limits. For the default tier, this is every budget member not in another tier: ```json theme={null} { "user_id": "user_abc123", "name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@example.com", "cycle_acu_limit_override": null, "temporary_cycle_acu_limit": 800, "effective_cycle_acu_limit": 800, "limit_source": "temporary_override", "membership": "explicit" } ``` * `cycle_acu_limit_override`: the user's permanent override, if any. * `temporary_cycle_acu_limit`: the user's temporary override, present only while it is live in the current monthly billing window. * `effective_cycle_acu_limit`: the limit currently enforced for the user; `null` means uncapped. * `limit_source`: where the effective limit comes from — `override` (permanent), `temporary_override`, or `tier`. * `membership`: why the user is in the tier — `explicit` (directly assigned), `idp_group` (via their winning IdP group mapping), or `default` (fallback to the default tier). ### Assign a user to a tier ```http theme={null} PUT /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/tiers/{tier_id}/users/{user_id} ``` Idempotent. Returns HTTP `204` on success. Moving a user from another tier clears any per-user override, so they start out inheriting the destination tier's limit. ### Remove a user from a tier ```http theme={null} DELETE /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/tiers/{tier_id}/users/{user_id} ``` Removes the user's explicit tier assignment (and any override). The user then resolves to their IdP-group-mapped tier, if any, else the default tier. Returns HTTP `204` on success. ## User endpoints ### Get a user's limits ```http theme={null} GET /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/users/{user_id} ``` Returns the user's resolved tier, limits, and pending request within the budget. Includes the [tier user fields](#list-a-tiers-users) above plus: ```json theme={null} { "tier_id": "tier-abc123", "tier_name": "Engineers", "tier_cycle_acu_limit": 500, "pending_request_id": null, "pending_request_cycle_acu_limit": null } ``` * `tier_id` / `tier_name`: the tier the user's limit resolves from (explicit assignment, IdP group mapping, or the default tier); `null` when the budget has no tiers. * `tier_cycle_acu_limit`: the tier's own limit before any override; `null` means uncapped. * `pending_request_id` / `pending_request_cycle_acu_limit`: the user's pending limit-increase request (its `request_id`, a string) and the limit it asks for, if any. ### Set or clear a user's override ```http theme={null} PATCH /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/users/{user_id} ``` User-scoped: the target only needs to be a budget member — no tier is involved, and the user's tier assignment is never changed. **Request body — set a temporary override** ```json theme={null} { "cycle_acu_limit": 800, "kind": "temporary" } ``` `kind` is required when setting a value: `permanent` never expires; `temporary` expires at the end of the current monthly billing window. **Request body — clear all overrides** ```json theme={null} { "cycle_acu_limit": null } ``` The endpoint returns HTTP `204` on success. ## IdP group endpoints Map an IdP group to a tier so its members inherit that tier automatically. Mappings are resolved live from group membership and never change a user's explicit tier assignment — an explicit assignment always wins. A user in several mapped groups resolves to the highest-ranked mapped tier (highest tier `priority`, ties broken by newest tier). ### List IdP group mappings ```http theme={null} GET /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/idp-groups ``` Returns a paginated list of the budget's group-to-tier mappings, oldest first. Filter with `?tier_id=` to list only groups mapped to one tier: ```json theme={null} { "idp_group_id": "grp_abc123", "idp_group_name": "Engineering", "tier_id": "tier-abc123" } ``` ### Get an IdP group's mapping ```http theme={null} GET /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/idp-groups/{idp_group_name} ``` Returns HTTP `404` if the group has no mapping in the budget. ### Map an IdP group to a tier ```http theme={null} PUT /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/idp-groups/{idp_group_name} ``` **Request body** ```json theme={null} { "tier_id": "tier-abc123" } ``` Idempotent upsert. The tier must belong to the budget. A group maps to at most one tier per budget, so mapping an already-mapped group moves it to the given tier. ### Unmap an IdP group ```http theme={null} DELETE /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/idp-groups/{idp_group_name} ``` Returns HTTP `204` on success. The mapped tier stops applying to the group's members; users with no explicit assignment and no other mapped tier fall back to the default tier. ## Limit-increase request endpoints Users can request a higher per-cycle limit. The requester's tier `policy` decides what happens: `unconditional` and `conditional` auto-approve up to the tier's `max_limit`, while `manual` holds the request for admin review through these endpoints. ### List limit-increase requests ```http theme={null} GET /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/{budget_id}/requests ``` Returns a paginated list of the budget's requests, filterable with `?status=` (`pending`, `approved`, `denied`, `expired`) and `?user_id=`: ```json theme={null} { "request_id": "42", "user_id": "user_abc123", "name": "Ada Lovelace", "email": "ada@example.com", "tier_id": "tier-abc123", "tier_name": "Engineers", "current_cycle_acu_limit": 500, "requested_cycle_acu_limit": 800, "message": "Wrapping up a large migration this month", "status": "pending", "created_at": 1735689600, "reviewed_at": null, "reviewer": null } ``` * `request_id`: a string. Pass it back unchanged in the request paths below. * `tier_id` / `tier_name`: the requester's tier within the budget; `null` when the budget has no tiers. * `current_cycle_acu_limit`: the limit currently enforced for the requester; `null` means uncapped. * `status`: `expired` means the request was still pending when its billing cycle ended. * `reviewer`: the admin who reviewed the request; `null` while pending. ### Get a limit-increase request ```http theme={null} GET /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/requests/{request_id} ``` ### Approve a limit-increase request ```http theme={null} POST /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/requests/{request_id}/approve ``` Grants the requested limit as a **temporary override** that expires at the end of the current monthly billing window. Optionally grant a different limit: ```json theme={null} { "cycle_acu_limit": 700 } ``` Returns the updated request. Returns HTTP `409` if the request was already reviewed or the requester is no longer an account member. ### Deny a limit-increase request ```http theme={null} POST /v3/enterprise/usage-policies/requests/{request_id}/deny ``` Returns the updated request, or HTTP `409` if it was already reviewed. ## Example workflows ### Set up a budget's tiers Find the budget, cap it at 2,000 ACUs a month, then create a default tier so every budget member gets a 500 ACU monthly cap: ```bash theme={null} curl "https://api.devin.ai/v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " curl -X PATCH "https://api.devin.ai/v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/budget-abc123" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"cycle_acu_limit": 2000}' curl -X POST "https://api.devin.ai/v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/budget-abc123/tiers" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"name": "Standard", "cycle_acu_limit": 500, "policy": "manual"}' ``` Map an IdP group to the tier and give one user a temporary bump for the rest of the month: ```bash theme={null} curl -X PUT "https://api.devin.ai/v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/budget-abc123/idp-groups/Engineering" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"tier_id": "tier-abc123"}' curl -X PATCH "https://api.devin.ai/v3/enterprise/usage-policies/budgets/budget-abc123/users/user_abc123" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"cycle_acu_limit": 800, "kind": "temporary"}' ``` ## Migrating from account-wide user limits User limits are moving from the account level to budgets. Your organization limits do not change unless you merge budgets (option 2). With user limits in budgets, each team can have its own limits, and group and user limits live in one place. Until your enterprise switches, your account-wide tiers and overrides keep applying. To migrate, you need to be an admin who can edit budgets. Open **Enterprise Settings** > **Usage policies**. At the top is the banner "User limits are migrating to per-budget user limits." Click the banner to show your budgets. ![Migration banner with the Enforce per-budget user limits switch and a table of budgets](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/ABQW9Vm6-2kyvMmW/images/admin/budgets/migration-helper.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=ABQW9Vm6-2kyvMmW\&q=85\&s=c80b438f91a610f79019fb32e1f1a156) The migration banner, expanded to show your budgets Choose one of the three options below, then [turn on enforcement](#turn-on-enforcement). ### Option 1: Copy user limits to each budget Select all budgets with the checkbox in the table header, then click **Copy user limits**. Before you confirm, Devin shows how many people would be blocked, based on their usage in the current billing cycle. ![Enforce per-budget user limits dialog showing how many users would be blocked](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/ABQW9Vm6-2kyvMmW/images/admin/budgets/migration-enforce-confirm.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=ABQW9Vm6-2kyvMmW\&q=85\&s=c093a3a4568a9095cd570d0a8fc2f0ff) Confirming enforcement, with the number of people who would be blocked The banner then reads "Per-budget user limits are in force." ![Banner reading Per-budget user limits are in force, with the switch on](https://mintcdn.com/cognitionai/ABQW9Vm6-2kyvMmW/images/admin/budgets/migration-enforced.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=ABQW9Vm6-2kyvMmW\&q=85\&s=d035f214116e812d1ce52a2410bff983) Per-budget user limits enforced When **Enforce per-budget user limits** is on, your account-wide tiers and overrides no longer apply. The older user-limit endpoints change meaning after the switch; see [What happens to the older user-limit endpoints?](#frequently-asked-questions) # Use your ChatGPT plan in Devin Source: https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/chatgpt Link your ChatGPT Go, Plus, or Pro subscription to Devin so GPT model usage in your sessions is billed to your ChatGPT plan instead of your Devin quota. If you have a ChatGPT subscription, you can link it to Devin and have the GPT model portion of your sessions billed to your ChatGPT plan instead of your Devin quota. Devin calls this **token sharing**: once your ChatGPT account is linked and the **Use your ChatGPT plan** switch is on, requests Devin makes to OpenAI models on your behalf draw from your ChatGPT plan's usage, and none of that usage counts against your Devin quota or on-demand credits. ## Eligibility * **ChatGPT plans:** You can share a personal ChatGPT **Go**, **Plus**, or **Pro** plan with Devin. You cannot share a Free plan, or a Business, Team, or Enterprise workspace account. * **Devin plans:** Token sharing is available on the [self-serve](/admin/billing/self-serve) **Pro**, **Max**, and **Teams** plans. It's not available on the Free plan or on Enterprise accounts. If you're on the Free plan, you'll see an **Upgrade your plan to connect ChatGPT** prompt in settings. ## Setup 1. Go to [Settings > Connections](https://app.devin.ai/account/connections) and choose **Continue with ChatGPT** to link your ChatGPT account. You'll be asked to sign in to ChatGPT and grant Devin permission to use your plan. 2. Check that **Use your ChatGPT plan** is on. The switch is on the same settings page, on the mode and model cards in the Devin Cloud picker, in the Devin Desktop model picker, and in Devin CLI (`/billing on`, or `Ctrl+S` in the `/model` picker). It's one switch for your account: changing it in one place changes it everywhere. You can unlink your ChatGPT account or turn the switch off at any time. ## What changes when it's on * **Devin Cloud:** Normal, Fast, Lite, Ultra, and Fusion sessions switch to GPT models so your ChatGPT plan can pay for them. If you pick a specific non-GPT model, the session stays on that model and is billed to your Devin quota. Fast mode isn't available while the switch is on. * **Devin Desktop and CLI:** Your model choice doesn't change. Requests to GPT models are billed to your ChatGPT plan; every other model is billed to your Devin quota. In the CLI, covered models are marked with an asterisk in the model picker. ## Check that it's working * **Devin Cloud:** Open the mode picker. The card shows **You're currently using your ChatGPT subscription** when your plan is in use. * **Devin CLI:** Run `/billing`. It shows **Use your ChatGPT plan: on**. * **Usage:** GPT usage paid by your ChatGPT plan appears in ChatGPT, not in Devin. Open [Settings > Usage & limits](https://app.devin.ai/settings/usage) and follow the **Manage usage** link to ChatGPT. ## What still uses your Devin quota Your ChatGPT plan pays only for GPT model requests in sessions you own. These still use your Devin quota or [on-demand credits](/admin/billing/self-serve#on-demand-credits): * Models other than GPT, including the non-GPT models in Fusion on Desktop and CLI, and any non-GPT model you pick yourself * Fast and priority GPT variants * The machine time of Devin Cloud sessions * Code scans * Sessions that aren't owned by you, such as automations that don't run as you Devin Cloud sessions also still need available Devin quota or on-demand credits to start, even when your ChatGPT plan pays for the models. ## FAQ ### What models can I use my ChatGPT plan with? You can use your ChatGPT plan with all GPT models available in Devin except fast and priority variants. ### How does my ChatGPT plan work with modes like Fusion or Adaptive? When your ChatGPT account is linked and **Use your ChatGPT plan** is on: * **Local Fusion (Devin Desktop and CLI):** When you choose a GPT model for Fusion, that model's usage is billed to your ChatGPT subscription. Usage from the other models is still billed to your Devin quota. * **Adaptive:** Adaptive automatically chooses models, so it only uses your ChatGPT subscription when it routes to a GPT model. Usage from other models is billed to your Devin quota. * **Cloud Fusion:** Cloud Fusion runs both its lead and its sidekick on GPT models, billed to your ChatGPT subscription. ### Is my ChatGPT subscription shared with Devin Cloud and Devin Desktop/CLI? Yes. Your linked ChatGPT subscription can be used across Devin Cloud, Devin Desktop, and Devin CLI. A single **Use your ChatGPT plan** toggle controls whether subscription sharing is active across all three products. Turning it on or off in one product applies everywhere; you don't need to link your ChatGPT account separately for each product. ### How does it work on the Teams plan? ChatGPT plans are linked per user, not per team. Each member of a Teams account can link their own ChatGPT subscription, and the sessions that member owns draw from their ChatGPT plan. There is no shared team-wide ChatGPT plan, and one member's linked plan is never used for another member's sessions. In a shared session, only the session owner can change the switch. ### Will I still consume Devin quota? Partly. GPT model requests are billed **only** to your ChatGPT plan and don't also consume Devin quota or on-demand credits. Everything listed in [What still uses your Devin quota](#what-still-uses-your-devin-quota) is billed to Devin as usual. ### What happens if I hit the limit on my ChatGPT plan? * **Devin Cloud:** The session pauses with the message **You've reached your ChatGPT subscription usage limit**. Devin doesn't move the session onto your Devin quota by itself. Resume the session once your ChatGPT limit resets, or turn off **Use your ChatGPT plan** and resume to continue on Devin usage. * **Devin Desktop and CLI:** A request that can't run on your ChatGPT plan is retried on your Devin quota, then on [on-demand credits](/admin/billing/self-serve#on-demand-credits), and you see a notice that your ChatGPT plan was unavailable. If your Devin quota is also used up, the request fails. ### Why does Devin say my ChatGPT connection has expired? Devin must have an active grant from your ChatGPT account to use your plan. If the grant expires or you revoke it, the Devin Cloud mode picker and [Settings > Connections](https://app.devin.ai/account/connections) show a message. The message is **Your ChatGPT connection has expired. Reconnect to use your plan.** Choose **Reconnect** in the mode picker to open Settings > Connections. Then link your ChatGPT account again. Until you do this, Devin Desktop and Devin CLI bill GPT requests to your Devin quota. # Enterprise Source: https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/enterprise How Devin Enterprise contracts are billed, how admins track ACU consumption, and how to set budgets and per-user ACU limits.
